methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: ODU and Google launch AI incubator to boost innovation in Hampton Roads - MSN
signals.signal_reading: ODU-Google AI incubator represents institutional infrastructure for peer-to-peer learning networks outside NoVA, potentially seeding regional AI fluency that could distribute capability beyond traditional tech corridors if sustained beyond initial launch.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Pressure on Richmond's young workforce signals that AI capability demands are concentrating in metro areas where knowledge work clusters, potentially accelerating brain drain from regions without comparable skill-building infrastructure.

signals.title: Blacksburg business owner: AI policy must work for small businesses
signals.signal_reading: Small business owner in Blacksburg highlighting policy disconnect reveals ground-truth adoption of platform AI tools in rural economies—shallow but pragmatic use without deep technical capability, fitting the distributed-but-shallow quadrant.

signals.title: When AI imagines cities, smaller communities can disappear - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech research finding that AI systems erase smaller communities from generated imagery serves as metaphor for concentration risk—if AI development centers ignore rural contexts, algorithmic bias could compound economic invisibility and limit distributed adoption pathways.

signals.title: U.Va. pilots three new artificial intelligence literacy courses - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: UVA piloting AI literacy courses across curriculum creates replicable educational infrastructure for building foundational fluency—if this model spreads to regional universities and community colleges, it could enable peer learning networks that distribute deep capability beyond initial elite institutions.
